page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-48-lssd is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Network Optimized family. The virtual hardware is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 180 GB of system memory, which allocates approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per compute core. The instance lacks discrete GPU acceleration and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, concentrating infrastructure resources entirely on high-capacity general computing and network-driven data delivery.

A defining hardware characteristic of the c4n-standard-48-lssd is its integrated storage subsystem. The server includes eight local NVMe SSDs that combine to provide 3,221 GB of high-speed local disk capacity. Because the storage is physically attached via the NVMe interface rather than mounted as networked block storage, it yields lower latency and sustained input-output throughput for heavy read and write operations directly on the host.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling 3,221 GB of high-speed NVMe storage directly with 48 dedicated cores reduces the necessity of provisioning expensive auxiliary network-attached storage tiers. However, operational tradeoffs must be considered: local NVMe storage is ephemeral, requiring application-level data replication or robust backup strategies to avoid data loss upon instance termination. The configuration represents an optimal fit for distributed databases, high-throughput caching tiers, real-time log ingestion, and big data analytical processing tasks requiring rapid scratch space.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-48-lssd is a network-optimized server configuration designed for data-intensive and communication-heavy workloads. Powered by an x86_64 architecture with 48 dedicated virtual CPUs, the platform provides consistent processor resources without hypervisor contention. It includes 180 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core, which suits balanced in-memory operations and multi-threaded processing. Integrated hardware storage consists of eight local NVMe SSDs totaling 3,221 GB of high-speed capacity, offering low-latency disk access for scratch space and distributed filesystems. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing purely on host-level compute, throughput, and local I/O performance. By coupling dense compute and high-capacity NVMe media into a unified envelope, the configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency by eliminating external block-storage bottlenecks. It is best deployed for high-performance databases, distributed analytics engines, caching clusters, and extensive input-output processing pipelines.
